card.name: Cuban Rumba
card.profile: Cuban rumba is a secular Afro-Cuban genre of music, dance and song that originated in urban Havana and Matanzas in the late 19th century, rooted in African (Abakua, Yuka/Congo) and Spanish-derived (coros de clave) traditions. The rumba complex comprises three forms: yambu (slow, couple), guaguanco (couple, featuring the vacunao pelvic thrust), and columbia (fast, solo, male, acrobatic, linked to Abakua). Performed with tumbadoras, lead quinto, claves, palitos/cata and call-and-response vocals (English Wikipedia; UNESCO).
card.insight: 'Rumba in Cuba' was inscribed on the UNESCO Representative List in 2016 (file 01185); UNESCO notes it historically acted as an expression of self-esteem and resistance (UNESCO).

parts.note: Guaguanco connecting basic steps & coordination to the rhythm

steps.name: Basic step in place
steps.description: Press with one foot and step without full weight change on the press.

steps.name: Side step
steps.description: Step out to the side while maintaining the press and weight transfer rhythm.

steps.name: Traveling forward/back
steps.description: Applying the basic in-place press and weight transfer while moving forward and backward.

steps.name: 3-step
steps.description: Step under your center with movement happening on counts 2 and 3.

cues: opposite arm drives the upper body movement
common_mistakes: losing chest posture when bending knees
making side steps massive and messing up weight transfer
safety: bent knees and hinging forward at the hip so you don't lose your chest
lessons.teacher_style: The instructor breaks down complex musical phrasing and rhythms using apps and clear verbal explanations. He demonstrates steps in front of a mirror with step-by-step breakdowns.
lessons.distinctive_method: Isolating each individual percussion instrument layer (clave, cata', shekere, tumba, tres-dos, quinto) and mapping specific body movements or weight transfers to each one before dancing.
what_works: breaking down each percussion instrument separately
showing footwork close-ups alongside mirror demonstrations
what_hinders: rhythm and musicality explanations can feel complex for beginners
